rationale: Registered the successor execution for the boundary case the account names as still open: a further election after healing. The healed-partition case now shuts down whichever instance led the healed cluster, waits two election windows, and reports how many instances lead afterwards together with the first index at which the two sides' stores still disagree and both sides' applied positions, so whether a later term reconciles the divergent committed content is observed instead of assumed. Construction-time local feedback is limited to compilation (go vet clean) because of the remaining turn budget; the case's earlier phases are unchanged and were executed in receipt 8c866b71bf0e470e900a15e895b2bed9.

scope.description: Whether a further election after a healed partition can reconcile the two sides' committed content. The predecessor's twenty-one cases are unchanged; the split_configurations case gains one phase: after the pre-heal split, the healing, the applied-state observation and the post-heal client entry, the instance that is in Leader state is shut down, the case waits twice its election window and then reports how many instances lead, the lowest index at which the restarted instance's store and the first peer's store still hold differing entries, and both sides' applied positions.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store; no instance is restarted or reconfigured after the healing, and the shutdown removes the healed leader only.
An instance applies its own store's entries up to the commit index it knows, so a side whose applied position has reached an index has applied whatever its own store holds there.
The compared stores are the restarted instance's and the first peer's, as in the applied-state phase, and the disagreement index is taken over the range they share.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crash injection, a snapshot taken or transferred after healing, application-level detection or repair, and any claim beyond the observed window about how the divergence ends.

experiment.prefix: Same case as the predecessor through the applied_state event: three peers, both non-leader peers demoted, 100 commands, a snapshot, both peers promoted, ten more entries, the leader disconnected and shut down, only it restarted with the case flag beside a fresh empty instance, both sides electing and committing uniquely named entries, the connections restored, the leader count and surviving entries reported, one client entry applied by whichever instance leads, and the applied_state event emitted. The case now additionally records whether that leader was the restarted instance, calls Shutdown on it, waits twice the election window, counts the instances in Leader state, re-runs probeFirstDivergence over the restarted instance's store and the first peer's store, reads both sides' applied positions (the minimum of the two peers'), and emits an applied_state_after_election CA_EVENT with the leader count, the disagreeing index if any, both applied positions, the derived divergent_applied_after_election field, and the wait.
experiment.responsibility: After healing, a later leader replicates its own entries over a term-matching prefix the follower already holds, and truncation follows a term mismatch only, so a further election does not by itself reconcile two sides whose committed content at one index differs under the same term.

comparisons.description: Healing with the flag enabled: the cluster is expected to converge on a single leader.
Healing with the flag enabled: only one of the two divergent committed entries is expected to remain.
Healing with the flag enabled: no two instances are expected to have applied different committed values for the same log index.
Healing with the flag enabled: a client entry applied after healing is expected to reach every instance's FSM.
Healing with the flag enabled, after the healed leader is shut down and a further election is allowed: no two instances are expected to hold different applied values for the same log index.
Control: with the flag disabled the sides never split, so no disagreeing index is expected after the election either.
Control: with the flag disabled the stores agree over the shared range, so no index holds two different applied values.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a post-healing election to the split_configurations case: after the applied-state phase the instance that led the healed cluster is shut down, the rest are left to elect, and the case reports the leader count, the first index at which the two sides' stores still disagree and both sides' applied positions, with a derived divergent_applied_after_election field. The comparison set adds this predicate for the flag-enabled case and its flag-disabled control to the six already recorded.
